key_insight: Removing viscous tilting of vorticity from DNS radically changes turbulence structure, showing that viscous reorientation is an essential part of Navier–Stokes turbulence.
engineering_relevance: Models or subgrid closures that ignore viscous tilting may miss key cascade physics and produce incorrect inertial-range behavior.
method: Directly modified direct numerical simulations of isotropic turbulence.
Surgically removed viscous tilting of vorticity while preserving the rest of the flow evolution.
Compared resulting vorticity alignment, stretching, and energy-spectrum scaling against standard turbulence behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a drastic structural change and a substantial departure from the -5/3 inertial-range energy spectrum when viscous tilting is removed.
watch_item: This is a controlled numerical intervention in isotropic turbulence, so the conclusion may not transfer unchanged to all flow types, Reynolds numbers, or practical modeling settings.
paper_title: Turbulence Without the Viscous Tilting of Vorticity
